entities.name: Leo I, Prince of Armenia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Leo I, also Levon I or Leon I, was the fifth lord of Armenian Cilicia (1129/1130–1137).

Born into a noble Armenian family, Leo I ascended to the throne in 1129 and ruled until his death in 1140. During his reign, he successfully defended the Armenian Cilicia against the Seljuk Turks and strengthened the region's economy through trade with neighboring kingdoms.

Leo I's legacy extends beyond his military prowess, as he also implemented significant administrative reforms, establishing a robust system of governance that would serve as a model for future Armenian rulers.

His rule marked the beginning of a golden age for Armenian Cilicia, with the region experiencing significant cultural, economic, and religious growth under his leadership.

Despite his many achievements, Leo I's life and reign remain somewhat of a mystery, with many details lost to the passage of time.

The 12th-century historian Steven Runciman once noted, "Leo I was a man of great energy and determination, who left an enduring legacy in the lands of his ancestors."
